issues.legal_issue: Rights arising under the laws of a territory before its conquest are not enforceable against the successor government unless that government recognizes them.
material_facts: A person obtained titles of manifest under the former sovereign’s mining laws and transferred them to the claimant before the territory was conquered.
The claimant applied for mining concessions under those laws before the conquest, but no concessions had been granted.
The successor government did not recognize the claimed entitlement and later stated that applications based on titles of manifest had lapsed.
issues.conclusion: The titles and pending applications did not give the claimant a right enforceable against the successor government because the claimed right had not been recognized by that government.
issues.legal_principle: On acquisition of territory by conquest, rights against the former sovereign do not pass to the new sovereign unless recognized. Continuing former laws does not itself recognize rights that arose under them; recognition may instead occur through a regrant, executive action, or a statutory saving provision that covers the rights in question. Section 5(1) of the Goa, Daman and Diu (Administration) Act, 1962 and section 4(2) of the Goa, Daman and Diu (Laws) Regulation, 1962 did not recognize rights arising before the conquest. The Court applied Pema Chibar v. Union of India and relied on the principle in Vajesingji Joravarsingji v. Secretary of State, followed in State of Gujarat v. Vora Fiddali and other cases.

rule.if: claim_to_enforce_pre_conquest_right_against_successor and territory_acquired_by_conquest and pre_conquest_right_claimed and not successor_recognized_right

predicates.claim_to_enforce_pre_conquest_right_agai: The proceeding seeks to enforce against a successor government a right claimed to have arisen under the former government.
predicates.territory_acquired_by_conquest: The territory in which the claimed right arose was acquired by another government through conquest.
predicates.pre_conquest_right_claimed: A person claims a right that arose under the former government’s laws before the territory was acquired.
predicates.successor_recognized_right: The successor government recognized the claimed right through a regrant, executive action, or applicable statutory protection.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks to enforce against a successor government a claimed right arising under a former government before the territory was acquired by conquest, the right is not enforceable if the successor government did not recognize it.

issues.legal_issue: Applications for mining concessions that remained pending when the new mining regime took effect had to be dealt with under that regime and could be deemed refused if not granted within the prescribed period.
material_facts: The claimant’s applications for mining concessions under the former mining laws remained pending when the new mining regime took effect.
The applications were not granted within the period specified by the new regime.
The claimant relied on the saving provision to argue that the applications could continue under the former laws.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming that the applications were pending when the new regime took effect, they had to be decided under the new Act and Rules and were deemed refused when not granted within the prescribed period.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(2) of the Goa, Daman and Diu (Laws) Regulation, 1962 did not preserve pre-conquest rights or entitle the claimant to have pending applications decided under the former mining laws. Section 4 and section 21 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, Rule 38 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, and Rule 24(3) supported application of the new regime and deemed refusal of applications not granted within the prescribed period. The Court applied Pema Chibar v. Union of India.

rule.if: mining_concession_application_proceeding and application_pending_when_new_regime_began and new_mining_regime_applied and not application_granted_within_prescribed_period

predicates.mining_concession_application_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an application seeking a mining concession.
predicates.application_pending_when_new_regime_bega: The application remained undecided when a new mining regime began to govern the territory.
predicates.new_mining_regime_applied: The new mining regime was made applicable to the territory and governed the application.
predicates.application_granted_within_prescribed_pe: The competent authority granted the application within the period allowed by the applicable regime.

issues.definition: A pending mining-concession application is deemed refused under the new regime when that regime governs the application and the application is not granted within its prescribed period.

issues.legal_issue: The rule concerning recognition of rights against a successor government applies even when competing private applicants dispute entitlement to a public concession.
material_facts: Two private applicants asserted competing claims to a mining lease over the same area.
One applicant’s claim depended on the successor government being obliged to recognize an alleged right arising under the former government’s laws.
The dispute therefore required determination of the successor government’s obligation, notwithstanding the presence of a private competitor.
issues.conclusion: The presence of a competing private applicant did not take the dispute outside the rule that a former-government right is enforceable against the successor government only if recognized by it.
issues.legal_principle: The substance of the claim, rather than the identity of the opposing litigant, determines whether the rule applies: the claim depended on whether the successor government was obliged to recognize the alleged former-law right. The Court applied Pema Chibar v. Union of India and rejected the argument that its principle was limited to disputes directly between the government and a citizen.

predicates.competing_private_concession_claimants: Two or more private applicants claim the same public concession.
predicates.claim_requires_successor_government_to_h: An applicant’s claim depends on the successor government being obliged to recognize a right allegedly arising under the former government’s laws.

issues.definition: When private applicants compete for a public concession and one claim depends on the successor government recognizing a former-law right, the private competition does not displace the recognition rule.
